hypotheses.text: In the foundational molecular and clinical cohort delineating OMIM #621474 (van Jaarsveld et al.), heterozygous pathogenic variants in KDM2B exhibit 100% penetrance for developmental delay and/or intellectual disability (21/21), whereas major structural congenital organ anomalies (cardiac, ocular, and urogenital) are each present in fewer than 60% of total individuals when non-CxxC truncating variants are pooled with CxxC missense variants.
hypotheses.rationale: Clinical delineation papers often report high aggregate rates for neurodevelopmental deficits while organ malformations vary by domain. Testing whether the original discovery cohort had 100% neurodevelopmental involvement but sub-60% individual organ penetrance resolves whether cardiac or renal anomalies can be treated as obligate diagnostic criteria.

evidence.text: The original delineation study identified a core cohort of 21 individuals with heterozygous (likely) pathogenic variants presenting consistently with developmental delay and/or intellectual disability, accompanied by variable congenital anomalies mainly of the heart, eyes, and urogenital system.

source.title: Delineation of a KDM2B-related neurodevelopmental disorder and its associated DNA methylation signature
source.quote: Our efforts resulted in a cohort of 21 individuals with heterozygous (likely) pathogenic variants. Individuals in this cohort present with developmental delay and/or intellectual disability; autism; attention deficit disorder/attention deficit hyperactivity disorder; congenital organ anomalies mainly of the heart, eyes, and urogenital system; and subtle facial dysmorphism.

numbers.metric: total individuals recruited with KDM2B variants

hypotheses.text: Within the specific KDM2B CxxC zinc finger domain sub-cohort (van Oirsouw et al., n=19), congenital heart defects have an exact frequency of 74% to 78% (14/19 to 15/19), establishing a significantly higher cardiac penetrance than the general KDM2B haploinsufficiency cohort.
hypotheses.rationale: van Oirsouw et al. directly compared CxxC domain variants against general KDM2B haploinsufficiency cases. Pinpointing the exact cardiac numerator and denominator (up to 78%) provides the precise statistical metric needed to identify CxxC-domain patients prior to sequencing.

evidence.text: In a cohort of 19 individuals carrying KDM2B CxxC domain variants, congenital heart defects were documented in up to 78% of individuals alongside 100% penetrance of developmental delay and variable intellectual disability.

source.title: KDM2B variants in the CxxC domain impair its DNA-binding ability and cause a distinct neurodevelopmental syndrome
source.quote: We analyzed clinical data from 19 individuals, including ten previously undescribed individuals with seven novel CxxC variants. The core phenotype of the KDM2B-CxxC cohort is more extensive as compared to that of individuals with KDM2B haploinsufficiency. All individuals with CxxC variants presented with developmental delay, mainly in the speech and motor domain... Congenital heart defects were observed in up to 78% of individuals

hypotheses.text: Renal structural anomalies (specifically unilateral renal agenesis or solitary dysplastic kidney) occur in exactly 33% (1/3) to under 45% of patients with CxxC domain variants, indicating that structural nephrourological abnormalities are an ancillary rather than an obligate feature of OMIM #621474.
hypotheses.rationale: OMIM #621474 designates variable renal abnormalities in its title, but exact numerators are required to assess whether absence of renal malformations can rule out the condition.

evidence.text: In a series of three children with confirmed KDM2B CxxC domain variants and diagnostic episignatures, exactly one of three (Patient 1) displayed a solitary kidney, while cardiac defects (ASD/VSD) were present in 2 of 3 and neurodevelopmental delay in 3 of 3.

source.title: KDM2B‐Related Neurodevelopmental Disorder A Case‐Series Supporting the CxxC Domain Phenotype With Emphasis on Ocular and Dermatologic Features
source.journal: American Journal of Medical Genetics Part A
source.quote: Patient 1 is a 2-year-old boy with developmental delay, solitary kidney, atrial septal defect, feeding difficulties, hemangiomas, and myopic astigmatism. Patient 2 is a 2-year-old girl with global developmental delay, hip dysplasia, feeding difficulties, hemangiomas, and myopic astigmatism. Patient 3 is a 5-year-old girl with autism, developmental delay, atrial septal defect, and ventricular septal defect, hypertrichosis, atopic dermatitis, and myopic astigmatism.

hypotheses.text: Across the aggregated 68-patient cohort reported by van Oirsouw et al. (2026), non-CxxC truncating loss-of-function and JmjC domain variants display incomplete penetrance (<50%) for the multisystem triad of cardiac, renal, and ocular malformations compared to the CxxC domain cluster, causing them to present primarily as non-syndromic neurodevelopmental delay.
hypotheses.rationale: van Oirsouw et al. (2026) analyzed 68 individuals (47 with confirmed (likely) pathogenic variants) and observed distinct facial gestalt and penetrance differences between CxxC and non-CxxC/JmjC variants.

evidence.text: Analysis of 68 individuals (37 variants in 47 individuals classified as pathogenic or likely pathogenic) demonstrated a highly penetrant CxxC-related phenotype with distinct facial features, contrasting with variable expressivity and incomplete penetrance of loss-of-function and JmjC domain variants.

source.title: Comprehensive Assessment of the KDM2B‐Associated Neurodevelopmental Disorder and the 12q24. 31 Microdeletion Syndrome
source.quote: We analyzed genotype-phenotype correlations of this cohort combined with previously reported individuals (n = 68) and classify 37 variants in 47 individuals as pathogenic or likely pathogenic. We observe a highly penetrant CxxC-related phenotype with distinct facial features supported by GestaltMatcher. In contrast, our findings point to variable expressivity and incomplete penetrance of loss-of-function variants and JmjC domain variants

new_directions.question_text: What are the exact sub-categorized cardiac anatomical subtypes (e.g., ASD vs VSD vs valve stenosis vs conotruncal anomalies) in the 47 pathogenic cases from van Oirsouw et al. (2026) to differentiate KDM2B from CHD7-associated heart malformations?
new_directions.rationale: CHARGE syndrome characteristically exhibits conotruncal defects and tetralogy of Fallot, whereas KDM2B reports frequently cite septal defects; extracting the exact sub-phenotype numbers will establish clear discriminating criteria.

new_directions.question_text: What is the exact incidence of anterior versus posterior segment structural eye anomalies (coloboma/microphthalmia vs refractive error/strabismus) in the CxxC vs non-CxxC cohorts across van Jaarsveld (2023), Ceroni (2026), and van Oirsouw (2026)?
new_directions.rationale: Clarifying whether coloboma is exclusive to the CxxC zinc finger domain will resolve whether ophthalmologic examination can pinpoint the variant domain before molecular sequencing.
